Check the spelling, or type the address instead.

Check the port, and that SSH or Rex is running there.
The machine could not be reached.
Check that the phone and the machine share a network, or that no firewall is in between.
No answer in time.
The machine may be off, asleep or behind a firewall. Try again.
This machine\'s host key has not been trusted yet.
Compare it with what ssh-keygen -lf prints on the machine before you trust it.
The host key is not the one trusted before.
Unless you know the machine was reinstalled or its key replaced, something may be in between: do not trust it.
SSH could not agree on a connection with the machine.
Its SSH server may be very old or allow only other ciphers.
There is no password or key to sign in with.
Type the password, or paste or pick the private key.
The private key could not be used.
Check the key, and its passphrase if it has one.
The machine refused the account, password or key.
Check the account name. For a key, add its public half to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the machine.
Rex is not installed on this machine, or not where the app looks.
Install Rex there: the app looks on the PATH and in ~/.local/bin.
Something answers on this port, but it is not Rex.
Check the port: Rex\'s plaintext one is 7297. Or connect over SSH.
The secure connection failed.
For Rex\'s plaintext port use ws://; for wss://, check the certificate.
Rex refused this phone.
Start Rex with --allow-anonymous on its plaintext port, or connect over SSH.
Rex did not answer in time.
Check that Rex is running on the machine: rex server status.
This Rex is too old: API revision %1$d, and the app needs %2$d.
Update Rex on the machine.
The connection failed.
The words under this say why. Try again, or send a report from Diagnostics.
